newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi meets unions over welfare reform.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi meets unions over welfare reform.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi, flanked by senior cabinet ministers, met Italian union leaders on Tuesday for the first round of talks over welfare reform in what promises to be a lengthy negotiating process.
Prodi was accompanied by his deputy, Walter Veltroni, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco and Labour Minister Tiziano Treu.
Unions were represented by the leaders of the big three labour federations.
Sergio Cofferati, head of the largest union, the Cgil, said on Monday that the first round of talks would be used to fix a timetable for subsequent meetings.

The government has pledged to introduce a reform of social expenditure by the end of the year with many economists urging structural spending cuts to bring about a lasting reduction of the state deficit.

European Union finance ministers on Monday called for Italy to introduce structural budget changes if it wanted to secure a place as a founder member of the planned single currency. Commentators said the comment referred to welfare spending.
However both the unions and the government's parliamentary ally, the hard-left Communist Refoundation, have said they will not brook any cut in social spending. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
